title: Intake filtering & micro-decommit plan — Sep 2026
content:
Context:
This is a working doc for a small, surgical backlog trimming pass focused on intake filtering and low-value UI features that are bleeding cycles. Objective: reclaim ~3 engineer-weeks for the upcoming sprint without impacting any customer SLAs or ongoing rollouts.

High-level constraints / guardrails:
- No change that touches auth, billing, or rollout core paths.
- Preserve any code paths behind customer-facing feature flags unless flagged explicitly for decommit.
- For items with telemetry uncertainty, prefer temporary feature flags + telemetry collection rather than immediate removal.
- Anything blocked on external dependency (infra change, infra budget request) is candidate for decommit unless it has an exec signoff.

Quick heuristics we used to score backlog items (sampling approach):
1) Usage signal (0-5): product analytics, support mentions in last 90d, NPS feedback.
2) Maintenance cost (0-5): # of open bugs + touch frequency in last 6mo.
3) Dependency risk (0-3): infra changes / cross-team coordination required.
4) Business tie (0-3): explicit OKR tie or revenue/enterprise asks.

Compute a lightweight priority score: (Usage * 2) + Maintenance cost - Dependency risk + Business tie. Low-scoring items (<6) moved to candidate decommit list.

Intake filtering rules to apply going forward (operational):
- New console intake tickets must include: expected user persona, telemetry plan (metric to validate success), rollback signal, and estimated touch points (FE + BE + infra). Tickets missing these fields auto-assign to "intake - clarify" queue and get 5 business days to be completed.
- Add a triage checkbox "backlog-proven" for items reintroduced from prior sprints: require a short note about why previous attempts failed.
- Introduce weekly 30m "micro-cut" meeting (product + eng lower-band reps) to review 6 lowest scoring items and decide to: keep, postpone with telemetry, or decommit.

Micro-decommit candidate list (recommendations):
- CON-1123: "Compact metric legend" (UI polish for Per-route dashboard) — score: 4.
  Rationale: low usage in telemetry (0.8% of sessions), causes repeated CSS frag regressions in 2 browsers. Recommendation: decommit and add short doc explaining how to re-add if requested. Owner: Marco Li.

- CON-1199: "Quick-share modal (deprecated provider flow)" — score: 5.
  Rationale: functionality for an old SSO flow used by <5 customers; significant test flakiness and maintenance overhead. Recommendation: schedule removal behind feature flag; set telemetry for 2 weeks; if no adoption, remove and archive assets. Owner: Eva Gomez.

- CON-1217: "Per-entity inline help tooltips (phase 2)" — score: 3.
  Rationale: Phase 1 shipped and provided most value; phase 2 is large and largely redundant. Recommendation: de-scope to a smaller doc update and remove UI work from this sprint. Owner: Samir Desai.

- CON-1255: "Desktop only keyboard shortcuts onboarding" — score: 2.
  Rationale: tiny usage on desktop apps; requires accessibility audit and adds QA matrix overhead. Recommendation: decommit; capture shortcuts in docs instead. Owner: Aisha Patel.

Action plan and timeline (3 working days):
Day 0 (today): finalize decommit list, assign owners, create a single decommit epic to track removals and doc the rollback plan.
Day 1: owners implement simple feature-flag gating or move code to archived modules (small PRs preferred).
Day 2: QA smoke checks and telemetry flags; update support articles + release notes draft.
Day 3: merge and close corresponding tickets; postmortem note in Confluence.

Wireframe & doc refs (quick notes):
- For the Compact metric legend removal, capture before/after screenshots: console-dashboard-v2/screenshot-legend-before.png and wireframe sketches for replacement placeholder. (linked_artifacts above references PR with image assets).
- For Quick-share modal, update the modal entry point to show a link to legacy flow docs if a customer hits it after removal.

Risks / unknowns / open questions:
- Several low-use features have intertwined unit tests that will need small maintenance work when removed; ensure we don't create a test vacuum that hides flakiness elsewhere.
- Enterprise customers: need to double-check if any of the flagged items were privately requested; check CS thread #enterprise-console-asks.
- Is decommit of keyboard shortcuts going to trigger an accessibility complaint? Liaise with accessibility lead before final removal.

Notes to self / followups:
- Add a new intake Jira template that forces the telemetry fields (quick patch to Jira admin).
- Bring a short summary to Monday's sync with Eng PMs (2 slides max).
- Set a reminder to check telemetry 2 weeks after gated removal for each decommit.

Decision log (short):
- 2026-09-10: Agreed to decommit CON-1123, CON-1217, CON-1255.  CON-1199 to be feature-flagged for 2 weeks before removal.

Quick checklist for owners before closing ticket:
- [ ] Add feature flag or move assets to /archived directory
- [ ] Update unit/integration tests to reflect removal
- [ ] Add an item to release notes
- [ ] Update support docs (or add link to legacy documentation)
- [ ] Post status in #console-product

If anything looks risky, escalate to product lead with tape of telemetry and support mentions.

-- End working draft --
